units.translation: ⟦1⟧ can be understood temporally, as at 83 and 291, but the sense is better taken as 'in general', cf. 52.
⟦1⟧ the aorist denotes the individual case: the general validity is expressed by ⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧ as ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, which here is expressed by ⟦6⟧ (⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, Frg. 103).
you may dishonor with a kick
having kicked the great altar of Justice
in time and on the appointed day, whoever among mortals dishonors the gods will pay the penalty
⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ (above all else, especially one's own desires).

⟦1⟧ (Heath) is an easy correction by transposition, so that (with ⟦2⟧) strophe and antistrophe are balanced; the other way of balancing requires a double correction: ⟦3⟧)⟦4⟧ (after Hermann) above and here (⟦5⟧)⟦6⟧ (Hartung), or, if ⟦7⟧, there (Herm.) ⟨⟦8⟧⟩ ⟦9⟧. ⟦10⟧ also stands ⟦11⟧ (cf. also Frg. 243. 264);
⟦1⟧ is perhaps to be taken proleptically, "so that thereby strangers are honored." On the double ⟦2⟧ Paley compares ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧. On these three foremost commandments see on V. 269 ff.
